english.notes: Figures are from the 2027/28 page (title 'English language requirements (2027/28)', last modified 14 October 2026), which applies to the September 2027 intake. Faculty of Science and Engineering bachelor's programmes, with 'Computing science' explicitly listed, require Admissions Level 1 (CEFR B2): IELTS Academic 6.0 overall and 6.0 in every band; TOEFL iBT 80 total on the pre-2026 scale (min. 18 Listening, 18 Reading, 20 Speaking, 21 Writing) or 4.0 total and per section on the new 1-6 scale for tests taken after 21 January 2026. Duolingo is not among the accepted tests on either the 2026/27 or 2027/28 page (not published -> omitted). NOTE the 2026/27 page set a higher bar for FSE (IELTS 6.5 overall, 6.5 every band; TOEFL iBT 90 with 21/21/21/24); the 2027/28 level is lower. The FSE-specific language page linked from the programme page returned HTTP 404 at three URL variants. value.description: No minimum GPA/grade threshold is published for Computing Science. Admission is by qualification equivalence: the applicant's secondary diploma must be equivalent to the Dutch pre-university (VWO) diploma; for Kazakhstan the university names the Nazarbayev Intellectual School (NIS) Grade 12 Certificate as VWO-equivalent, plus a subject-specific Mathematics requirement assessed by the Admissions Board from course descriptions. Applications are assessed individually. A GPA remark on the Kazakhstan page appears only under the Faculty of Law, not under Science and Engineering.

scholarship_exists.how_found: Search: site:rug.nl scholarship international bachelor students University of Groningen -> NL Scholarship page (the 'holland-scholarship' URL redirects to the same page). Second search: site:rug.nl/education/scholarships bachelor non-EU scholarship University of Groningen (found only the same scheme plus programme-specific Campus Fryslan awards).
scholarship_exists.notes: CAVEAT 1 (governance): the NL Scholarship is co-financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education and the Dutch universities; the University of Groningen selects, ranks and pays its own awardees ('NL Scholarship University of Groningen'), so it is university-administered rather than purely external government aid, but it is not a UG-only fund. CAVEAT 2 (level): the page's structured 'Purposes' field lists 'Bachelor (BSc/BA/LL.B)' and 'Programmes: All', but its narrative sentence says the scholarship is for students 'who want to do their master's in the Netherlands' - the page is internally inconsistent on bachelor eligibility; confirm with the Mobility Scholarship Desk. No other UG-run scholarship open to incoming non-EU bachelor applicants in Computing Science was found: the bachelor 'Financial matters' page names none, the Grantfinder requires JavaScript, and the other hits (University College Fryslan Foundation scholarship, Campus Fryslan non-EU scholarships) are restricted to Campus Fryslan programmes. Page last modified 28 September 2026; no academic year stated. In quotes, ' | ' marks a table-cell or element boundary in the page markup; the text inside each cell is copied exactly.

See the bachelor-vs-master wording caveat under scholarship_exists.

access_notes: The FSE English-language page linked from the programme page (https://www.rug.nl/fse/education/admission-application/apply-bsc/language) returned HTTP 404; the variants /fse/education/admission-and-application/apply-bsc/language?lang=en and /fse/programme/admissions/bsc/language?lang=en also returned 404. Scores were taken from the central university language-requirements pages instead, which list Computing Science by name.
https://www.rug.nl/bachelors/computing-science/ without ?lang=en renders in Dutch ('Informatica'); the English version was used for all quotes.
The Grantfinder (https://www.rug.nl/grantfinder -> /education/scholarships/findscholarships) shows only a search form without JavaScript; results were not retrievable.

The URLs .../education/bachelor/international-students/financial-matters/nl-scholarship and .../holland-scholarship redirect to the generic tuition-fee page; the scholarships overview page (/education/scholarships/) is generic and last modified in 2019.
Pages were fetched with WebFetch and with curl (raw HTML saved locally) so that quotes could be verified character-for-character against page text; all quotes passed that check.
No login was used and no robots or block was bypassed.
